newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tchibo says too early to detail coffee strategy.
newsitem.headline: Tchibo says too early to detail coffee strategy.

text.p: Tchibo Holding AG cannot yet specify details of implementing its purchase of Bremen-based coffee roasting firm Eduscho GmbH & Co, a spokeswoman said after the cartel authority approved the merger on Tuesday.
"We've only establishing contact now...after all we were competitors until yesterday," she said.
After studying the merger plans for four months, the German cartel office said Tchibo could buy 100 percent of Eduscho, retroactive to January 1, 1997.

A Tchibo statement said the two companies would now start talking about joint restructuring programmes, which would form the economic basis for future activities in their tied retail outlets, which sell coffee and consumer goods.
The strategic goal was to expand on the strengths of both companies which would be maintained and managed separately.
Tchibo coffee sales in 1996 were estimated at 3.50 billion marks and Eduscho's at 2.25 billion, Tchibo has said.
Traders believe the move could create a powerful raw materials customer, which could try and exert downward pressure on buying prices.
"They could try and use economies of scale and find powerful trade partners to supply coffee in bulk,...this could be difficult for small and medium-size traders," one said.
"I would also imagine more intense competition in the retail markets as and when the two companies refocus their wide range of coffee and non-food product offers."
Competitor and market leader Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS), part of Philip Morris Inc saw the move as ultimately positive, spokesman Rolf Sauerbier said from the company's Bremen headquarters.
He said the strategy of a larger company should be more calculable than the moves of fragmented small operators.
"We are planning to secure and expand our growing market share independent of competitors' moves," he also said.
"We'll keep a close eye on the developments but we won't draw up an anti-Eduscho/Tchibo strategy and instead focus on our strengths -- growth of our flagship Kroenung range and coffee specialities."
He estimated the KJS share of German roasted coffee sales in the first quarter of 1997 at 30 percent and put Tchibo/Eduscho at 25 to 26 percent.
